articleTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Day on Diffraction 2006
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: light propagation; creeping waves; inverse problem of acoustic wave propagation; split-step Fourier method; nonlinear Schrodinger equation; flexural plane wave scattering; coherent states of Krawtchouk oscillator; source-excited electromagnetic fields; negative dispersion cylindrical surface plasmon-polaritons; variational principle in dissipative hydrodynamics; and parametric instability of electromagnetic surface waves

articleTitle: RCS computation in near field
abstract: This communication presents a physical optics based method developed by CELAR to calculate radar cross section (RCS) in function of the distance separating the target and the radar system. Initially this method has been developed to calculate RCS in the same geometrical configurations than the measurements performed in the CELAR facilities. So, after a short presentation of RCS measurement facilities of CELAR, this paper will expose the method developed to calculate near field RCS. Comparisons between measurements and calculations will be shown to validate the method. Then, some applications will be given on canonical and complex targets. For flat circular and square plates, particular phenomena will be detailed and some analytical approximated formula will be proposed to express their monostatic specular RCS

articleTitle: Wavelet analysis for the solutions of the wave equation
Electromagnetic waves generated by line exponentially decaying current pulses
abstract: Electromagnetic pulses emanated by exponentially decaying currents propagating along a finite line segment with subluminal and luminal velocities are considered. Corresponding electromagnetic problem for the decaying unit-step current is solved by incomplete separation of variables and the basic solution is obtained for the magnetic field strength. This solution is a sum of an analytical expression and a quadrature term, the latter admitting good analytical approximation in the far zone (r/lgsim10), where the entire electromagnetic field can be assessed. Eventually, the results of this work represent feasible analytical expressions for the electromagnetic-pulse durations and maximum amplitude for different configurations of the source, including such practical models as a bipolar current and a current pulse partially reflected from the radiator end

articleTitle: Gaussian beam migration of multi-valued zero-offset data
Split-step Fourier method for nonlinear Schrodinger equation
An analytical way of the fundamental cavity mode construction
abstract: In this work the analytical way of the fundamental cavity mode construction is proposed. It in not necessary to find eigenvectors of the monodromy matrix. The algorithm can be used both to obtain explicit formulae for Gaussian beam and to perform numerical calculations. The procedure offered consists in sequential simplification of a problem using homothetic transformations to reduce it to one of basic variants being solved explicitly-in some cases as a continuous set of matrices. The correspondence between these variants and spectral characteristics of an initial monodromy matrix is established

articleTitle: Nonstationary scattering DN-problem of a plane wave by a wedge
Diffraction by a strongly elongated object illuminated by an electromagnetic plane wave propagating in the paraxial direction -- application to a prolate ellipsoid
abstract: Following the asymptotic theory of creeping waves on a strongly elongated object, developed by Andronov and Bouche [1], the authors have derived explicit formulas for the asymptotic currents on a strongly elongated object excited by an electromagnetic plane wave propagating in the paraxial direction. Numerical results for the asymptotic currents along the geodesics followed by the creeping waves will be shown and compared to the results obtained by solving the EFIE.

articleTitle: On the variational principle in dissipative hydrodynamics
Temperature dependence of surface electromagnetic wave attenuation for nickel
Hamilton-jacobi-bellman equations for quantum optimal control
abstract: One develops a Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation and a stochastic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation for quantum optimal feedback control. In this paper we do not discuss in details how to find the optimal control functions; we would like to notice only that the corresponding generalizations of the classical Pontryagin maximum principle can be obtained and used

articleTitle: On the Nonlinear Spectral Problem
Validity and naturalness of definitions of /spl delta/- and /spl delta/-shock type solutions to systems of conservation laws
abstract: Generalizing the classical definition of a weak L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">infin</sup>-solution definitions of delta- and delta'-shocks for systems of conservation laws were introduced and the Cauchy problems admitting such singular solutions were solved. In this paper we discuss and substantiate the validity and naturalness of the above-mentioned definitions. As these definitions differ from the classical definition of a weak L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">infin</sup>-solution, this problem is important

articleTitle: Negative dispersion cylindrical surface plasmon-polaritons in spatially inhomogeneous dielectric permittivity media
abstract: The investigation of surface plasmons properties and propagation in left-handed media is significant problem in area of surface physics in recent years. The existence and propagation of surface plasmon polaritons in cylindrical geometry for the case of the spatially inhomogeneous dielectric permittivity of cylinder in comparison with homogeneous one has been investigated. The application of obtained results is discussed

articleTitle: Geometrical degeneration of creeping waves on an anisotropic surface
Flexural plane wave scattering by the thin elastic quarter plane in the case of pinched boundary
Confluence of free boundaries as a result of nonlinear waves interaction
Smolyanov surface measures and solutions of Schroedinger and heat type equations on a Riemannian manifold
abstract: In the paper we give solutions of Schroedinger and heat type equations on a Riemannian manifold in the form of functional integrals over Smolyanov surface measures on the set of trajectories in a manifold and over the Wiener measure, generated by Brownian motion in the manifold. These integrals are in fact limits of finite-dimensional integrals (over Cartesian products of some copies of the manifold) of elementary functions containing coefficients of equations, initial conditions and geometric characteristics of the manifold. In the proof, a substantial role is played by Smolyanov-Weizsaecker-Wittich asymptotic estimates for Gaussian integrals over a manifold, by the Chernoff theorem and by the method of transition from the Schroedinger to the heat equation going back to Doss

articleTitle: Quantization conditions for the vector Sturm-Liouville problem
Scattering of electromagnetic impulse on the standing ion-acoustic wave forced by the powerful electromagnetic wave in the liner plasma layer
Natural oscillations of a rectangular acoustic volume with elastic walls
Negative dispersion cylindrical surface plasmon-polaritons in layered media
Strong asymptotic completeness for quantum wires
Singularity formation for a pressureless gas dynamics system of conservation laws
Many particles problems for quantum layers
abstract: In quantum computer implementation using resonance phenomena in quantum waveguides coupled through small windows is suggested. It has some interesting features, but faces some objectives. There are two variants of such devices. In the first one we have two quantum waveguides for each qubit, and the state of the qubit is determined by the position of the electron. In the second variant we have one waveguide for each qubit and the state of the qubit is determined by the electron spin projection ("up" or "down"). In each case, to perform many-qubit operations successfully, we need to solve the two-electrons problem in the area of waveguide and to synchronize the electrons in different waveguides. Also preparation of the initial state is here very important problem. In the present paper we study the Green function for the simplest cases of two noninteracting particles in two-dimensional infinite straight waveguide and three-dimensional infinite layer with Neumann boundary conditions. We use the convolution method based on known representation of the one-particle Green function

articleTitle: Use of asymptotic solutions of differential approximations for improvement of the schemes
Transient waves produced by a periodically expanding sphere
Light propagation in helicoidal media with large periodicity
The fields generated by finite grating coupler in conditions of SEW excitation
abstract: The problem of surface electromagnetic waves (SEW) excitation by finite size grating was studied theoretically. It was shown that in conditions of SEW launching the pressed waves (near surface bulk waves) generated on the smooth part of metal surface which is in conjunction with earlier experimental observations

articleTitle: Inverse problem of acoustic wave propagation in a structure with weak lateral inhomogeneity
Parametric instability of electromagnetic surface waves guided by the isotropic plasma slab - chiral medium boundary
abstract: The linear stage of parametric instability of surface waves guided by the interface between chiral medium and planar isotropic plasma slab on the metallic substructure is investigated. This instability can arise due to the presence of an intense electric field, which is perpendicular to the boundary. The growth rate for the instability of surface waves and the threshold amplitude of incident wave are determined

articleTitle: Some solutions to the wave equation in the case of temporal dependence of the source-pulse velocity
abstract: An algorithm for constructing some solutions to the wave equation for arbitrary temporal dependence of the velocities of the source-pulse front and back are given. Two specific solutions of the initial-value problem of wave formation for sub- and superluminal hyperbolic motion of the source are obtained and discussed

articleTitle: Nonstationary problem of thin elastic plate oscillations
abstract: In this paper, we consider the oscillations of thin elastic plate excited by vertical forces applied to the both sides of plate with the same distribution. The solution of this problem is obtained by solving the 2D-problem in space. The properties of the dispersion equation, the asymptotics of field and the elastic plate approximation are obtained

articleTitle: Extended wave propagators as pulsed-beam communication channels
abstract: Let P(x<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>-x<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub>) be the causal propagator for the wave equation, representing the signal received at the spacetime point x<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> due to an impulse emitted at the spacetime point x <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub>. Such processes are highly idealized since no signal can be emitted or received at a precise point in space and at a precise time. We propose a simple and compact model for extended emitters and receivers by continuing P to an analytic function Pmacr(z<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>-z<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub>), where z<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub>=x<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub>+iy<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub> represents a circular pulsed-beam emitting antenna centered at x<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub> and radiating in the spatial direction of y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub> while z<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>=x<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>-iy<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> represents a circular pulsed-beam receiving antenna centered at x<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> and receiving from the spatial direction of y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>. The space components y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub>,y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> of y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub>,y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> give the spatial orientations and radii of the antennas, while their time components s<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub>, s<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> represent the time a signal takes to propagate along the antennas between the center and the boundary. The analytic propagator Pmacr represents the transmission amplitude, forming a communication channel. Causality requires that the extension/orientation 4-vectors y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub> and y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> belong to the future cone V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sub>, so that z<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub> and z<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> belong to the future tube and the past tube in complex space-time, respectively. The imaginary "retarded time" T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub>=s <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub>-|y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub>|/c represents the duration of the emitted pulse, and T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>=s<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>-|y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>|/c represents the integration time for the received pulse. The bandwidths of the antennas are 1/T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub> and 1/T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>, respectively. The invariance of Pmacr under imaginary spacetime translations (z<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub>rarrz<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub>+ieta, z<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>rarrz<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r </sub>+ieta) has nontrivial consequences
